content.title: About
content.content: Bean chips are crunchy snacks made from whole beans (such as soy, chickpeas, or lentils) that are baked or fried until golden. They have a rich nutty flavor, a light salty aroma, and contain little to no added sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bean chips provide more plant protein than most traditional potato chips.
Production often uses whole beans, preserving most of the dietary fiber.
Beans are a natural source of complex carbohydrates that release energy slowly.
Compared to potatoes, bean chips usually have a lower glycemic index.
Flavor varieties include sea salt, smoked paprika, garlic, cheese, and spicy chili.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Bean chips contain 15–20 % protein, helping maintain muscle mass and promote satiety.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion, blood‑sugar regulation, and gut microbiota.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The slow digestion of beans prevents rapid spikes in blood glucose after eating.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: They provide thiamine, riboflavin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of beneficial minerals
items.content: Bean chips supply iron, magnesium, and potassium, supporting heart and muscle function.

items.title: Bean allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy, chickpeas, or other beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salted versions can contain significant sodium, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although generally lower in calories than potato chips, portion control is still advisable.

items.title: Anti‑nutrients
items.content: Certain beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bean chips are perfect as a standalone snack, tossed into salads, soups, or used as a crunchy topping for dishes. Pair them with yogurt‑based dips, guacamole, or hummus for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent fat oxidation.
